newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil re-election to go to vote next week - whip.
newsitem.headline: Brazil re-election to go to vote next week - whip.

text.p: Brazil's government intends to hold next week a first full vote in the Chamber of Deputies on a bill that would allow President Fernando Henrique Cardoso to stand for re-election, a government whip said.

"We are going to put the (re-election) amendment to a vote next week although the exact day has not yet been decided," Dep. Inocencio Oliveira, lower house leader of the government-allied Liberal Front Party (PFL), said.

Oliveira's comments contrasted with general expectations of when the government could put re-election to a first vote on the floor of the lower house, given opposition within the powerful Brazilan Democratic Movement Party (PMDB).

The PMDB, the largest party in Congress and without whose votes the government cannot muster the three-fifths majorities needed for re-election on the lower house floor, is split on whether or not to support re-election.

An anti-government wing of the party has insisted PMDB lawmakers must observe a convention recommendation not to vote on re-election until Feb. 15, after upcoming elections in both houses of Congress which the PMDB wants to win.

Oliveira said the government was confident it had enough support in the Chamber of Deputies to get the two three-fifths majorities it needs to approve the constitutional amendment allowing re-election in the lower house.

However, negotiations between the government and the parties that make up its multi-party alliance in Congress were due to take place later on Thursday and on Friday to ensure victory, Oliveira said without specifically mentioning the PMDB.

On Wednesday, Oliveira suggested the PMDB might agree to vote on re-election in a first vote on the floor of the Chamber of Deputies next week in return for a government agreement not to put the bill to its second and final vote after Feb. 15.
By not giving re-election its final approval in the lower house until after Feb. 15, the PMDB might maintain the spirit of its convention recommendation, the whip said on Wednesday.

Cardoso called a special session of Congress to run through the January recess in the hope of getting re-election approved before the pro-reform president of the Chamber of Deputies, Dep. Luiz Eduardo Magalhaes, steps down on Feb. 1.
The government also wants re-election approved quickly in order to resume progress on its social security, civil service and tax reforms which have been put on hold.
